# The postcard bodies that cross a runtime boundary, pinned as bytes: the
# activation a host decodes, the result it encodes, and the effect record,
# park and correction bodies the controller decodes off a runner's frames.
#
# Four runtimes read this file and none derives it. `flz_core` encodes every
# row from the real struct (`flz_core/src/postcard_bodies_tests.rs`) and fails
# on a row it does not produce or one the file lacks; the controller decodes
# the effect, park and correction rows through `Flezha.State.Wire`, and its
# test encoders write the effect and park rows back
# (`test/flezha/state/wire_test.exs`); Java's `ActivationCodecTest` and PHP's
# `SchemaFixtureTest` encode and decode the activation and result rows.
#
# Provenance: TRANSCRIBED BY HAND from one run of the Rust encoders at
# `6816b368` and checked in. A golden a runtime derives at test time is not a
# golden, it is a second copy of the thing under test.
#
# Postcard writes integers as LEB128 varints, a `Vec` or `String` as its varint
# length and then its items, a struct or tuple as its fields in declaration
# order, an `Option` as `00` or `01` and the value, and an enum as its variant
# index and then its fields. Field order IS the wire.
#
# One row per case, `|`-separated: type | case | hex. The values each case
# encodes are spelled in `flz_core/src/postcard_bodies_tests.rs`.
#
# Command activations are all token 1 addressed to relay `o`, tasklet 0, no
# key, change seq 0, factory `f` and no identity, so each starts `01016f0000` and
# ends `00016600`. The work activation carries the identity `id` and its input
# the form `transformed`.
